plan.title: Liver 3-group DE: LRT + pairwise treated vs control
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is a bulk RNA-seq liver experiment with 3 groups (control, treated_a, treated_b), 4 replicates each, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon-derived gene-level counts (12000 genes x 12 samples). The research question has two parts: (1) which genes differ across all three groups at all (an omnibus test), and (2) which genes each treatment changes relative to control (two pairwise contrasts). This maps directly onto a single DESeq2 model with 'condition' as the only factor: a likelihood-ratio test (LRT) against the reduced intercept-only model answers the omnibus question, and Wald tests with contrasts (treated_a vs control, treated_b vs control) answer the pairwise questions. All three tests are fit from one DESeq2 object built once, so dispersion estimation is shared and consistent across tests. QC (library size, PCA, sample clustering) precedes modeling to confirm no batch/outlier issues before trusting the design as stated. Downstream, the two pairwise DE gene sets and the LRT gene set are each sent to pathway overrepresentation analysis using the human WikiPathways gene sets available in the reference store, and a comparison step characterizes shared vs treatment-a-specific vs treatment-b-specific responses.
